how: power_table.py: for each stop and shape, cost in R from fees.py, then power_mde (two-sided, alpha 0.05) gives the fills needed for 80 % power and the smallest net edge each sample size can see. Re-run: python power_table.py --sim-json <file>.
window: none yet (a gate computed before any data is read); rule runs will use DEV 2022-04-01..2024-06-30

verdict.label: Not run yet: harness ready, waiting for the caption extracts

why: 6 of 12 stop / shape cells lose after fees alone (net <= 0 R), including every 0.3 % stop: tight-stop rules need a large RR to survive.
A 27-month DEV swing rule with 50-300 fills only detects a net edge of about 0.3-0.5 R; smaller edges read NOT ENOUGH DATA, not PASSED.
Each Rumers rule gets its own card here when it runs, with example trades on the chart.
